family.description: This family includes four different proteins from E. coli alone. One of them, YdgG or TqsA, has been shown to mediate transport of the quorum-sensing signal autoinducer 2 (AI-2). It is not clear if TqsA enhances secretion of AI-2 or inhibits AI-2 uptake. By altering the intracellular concentration of AI-2, TqsA affects gene expression in biofilms and biofilm formation [[cite:PUB00076990]]. TsqA belongs to the AI-2 exporter (AI-2E) superfamily [[cite:PUB00076989]].
family.name: AI-2E family transporter

causal_graphs.context: Overnight donor cultures are diluted 1:100 in LB and harvested at OD600 0.6. Filter-sterilized supernatants are assayed with V. harveyi BB170 luminescence normalized per reporter cell. The cited detailed reporter protocol was not independently inspected; no absolute AI-2 concentration or reporter incubation time is invented.

evidence.explanation: AI-2 Methods p. 589 and extracellular-activity Results p. 590 provide the LB comparison and reporter endpoint; Discussion retains export-versus-uptake alternatives.
Current reference mapping supports the gene/domain association, not identity of every historical construct or isolated-domain causality.

edges.mechanism: The WT/knockout extracellular activity ratio is reported as 13 +/- 9 in LB. The deletion decreases this reporter endpoint; it does not directly prove TqsA-mediated AI-2 export or a domain-specific reaction.
edges.subject: tqsa-deletion-lb

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P0AFS5 / tqsA/ydgG / b1601 is the 344-aa K12 reference, sequence version 1, with PF01594 17-328. The paper identifies b1601/ydgG and verifies the complete BW25113 deletion by five PCRs. Reference sequence and InterPro match exactly, but the historical assay strain/clone was not independently sequenced. Deletion removes the whole gene, not only the domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: Reporter activity is not a direct chemical concentration or membrane flux. Pleiotropy, polarity and altered signal production/uptake remain possible. This assay cannot distinguish increased export from decreased uptake; the later structural study did not demonstrate TqsA transport with its attempted methods.

evidence.explanation: Extracellular-activity Results p. 590 distinguish the 4 +/- 2 LBglu ratio from the 13 +/- 9 LB ratio; Methods define donor sampling and the reporter.

edges.mechanism: WT supernatant produces 4 +/- 2 times the knockout reporter activity in LBglu. The retained direction is a deletion effect on the measured reporter response, not a direct TqsA export step.
edges.subject: tqsa-deletion-lbglu

causal_graphs.family_mapping: b1601/ydgG maps to P0AFS5, 344 aa, PF01594 17-328; the intervention replaces the entire BW25113 gene with a kanamycin cassette. K12 reference identity is not independent historical clone resequencing.
causal_graphs.limitations: This indirect bioassay does not establish absolute extracellular AI-2, protein-mediated flux or a single transport direction. Glucose changes regulatory context; the LB result is not substituted for this condition.

causal_graphs.context: LB plus 0.2% glucose; overnight cultures are diluted to obtain exponential cells at OD600 0.6 and stationary cells at OD600 6. Beta-galactosidase activity is reported as ONPG cleavage per minute per protein mass. Figure 3 uses duplicate experiments and SD; the two phases remain separate endpoints.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 3 and Results p. 591 support the exponential LBglu comparison; AI-2 Methods p. 589 identify the reporter and OD600 endpoint.

edges.mechanism: The knockout/WT lsr reporter ratio is 16 +/- 5 under exponential LBglu conditions. Increased beta-galactosidase is observed; the implied intracellular AI-2 change is not a direct chemical measurement.
edges.subject: tqsa-deletion-exponential

evidence.explanation: Figure 3's stationary LBglu bars and Results p. 591 establish the increase under the independently specified OD600-6 condition.

edges.mechanism: At stationary phase the knockout/WT lsr reporter ratio is 10 +/- 5. This separate endpoint is not treated as a time-resolved mechanistic transition from the exponential-phase measurement.
edges.subject: tqsa-deletion-stationary

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The complete BW25113 ydgG deletion maps at gene level to 344-aa P0AFS5, whose current PF01594 domain spans 17-328. The reporter plasmid is a separate assay entity and does not measure the isolated domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: lsr transcription is an indirect intracellular-signal proxy affected by regulatory context, including glucose catabolite repression. The authors propose a future luxS/ydgG double-mutant test; AI-2 mediation is not uniquely established. No intracellular chemical concentration, export velocity or serial reporter-to-biofilm chain is inferred.

causal_graphs.context: Cultures receive IPTG and 30 ug/ml chloramphenicol, are harvested at OD600 0.6, washed twice for 10 min at 8820g to remove antibiotic that inhibits the Vibrio reporter, and resuspended in 20 ml LB plus 0.2% glucose. Supernatants are sampled after growth to OD600 0.9. The retained endpoint is 1.5 mM IPTG, compared with the uncomplemented/vector context and normalized to WT with pCA24N.

evidence.explanation: Complementation Methods p. 589 and Results p. 591 explicitly state the wash/regrowth protocol, empty-vector comparator, dose series and restoration endpoint.

edges.mechanism: Induced ydgG expression increases the deletion strain's extracellular reporter activity toward the WT-empty-vector level; the reported complemented/WT ratio at 1.5 mM IPTG is 1.0 +/- 0.3. This is genetic support for the phenotype, not resolution of export versus uptake.
edges.subject: induce-tqsa-complement

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The historical pCA24NydgG+ expresses the b1601/ydgG gene corresponding to P0AFS5, PF01594 17-328. Full historical tag/linker sequence is not established. Gene-level trans-complementation does not isolate the domain or rule out every overexpression-mediated effect.
causal_graphs.limitations: Restoration concerns the extracellular BB170 bioassay only; it is not direct export, restoration of intracellular lsr output or a universal rescue of all deletion phenotypes. Washed OD600-0.9 cultures must not be merged with the plasmid-free OD600-0.6 comparisons.

evidence.explanation: The 96-well Methods p. 588 and initial biofilm Results p. 589 support this LBglu ratio, not the much larger flow-cell ratios.

edges.mechanism: The knockout/WT staining ratio is 3.8 +/- 0.2 in LBglu. This assay-specific increase is not proof that TqsA directly represses a molecular biofilm pathway or that every medium has the same response.
edges.subject: tqsa-deletion-biofilm-lbglu

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Complete ydgG replacement affects the whole P0AFS5-associated gene, including PF01594 17-328 and its flanks; the current reference is 344 aa and gene-matched to BW25113, not independently clone-sequenced.
causal_graphs.limitations: Staining is an attached-mass proxy, not a uniquely AI-2-mediated mechanism or direct domain activity. The paper reports separate trans-complementation with different antibiotic/induction conditions; that is not silently substituted into this plasmid-free comparison. The direction reverses in unsupplemented LB.

record.description: This family includes four different proteins from E. coli alone. One of them, YdgG or TqsA, has been shown to mediate transport of the quorum-sensing signal autoinducer 2 (AI-2). It is not clear if TqsA enhances secretion of AI-2 or inhibits AI-2 uptake. By altering the intracellular concentration of AI-2, TqsA affects gene expression in biofilms and biofilm formation [[cite:PUB00076990]]. TsqA belongs to the AI-2 exporter (AI-2E) superfamily [[cite:PUB00076989]].

evidence.explanation: Eight observed indirect effects retain separate extracellular, intracellular-proxy, complementation and medium-specific staining contexts. The exact historical clone, initial well-assay time/temperature and detailed reporter protocol remain open. Other motility, flow-cell and complementation endpoints require separate curation; MIC ordering is ambiguous.

The 2022 Discussion explicitly reports inability to demonstrate TqsA transport with attempted methods. Native-MS binding and proposed structural movement do not supply an observed transmembrane step. Preliminary mutants, the suspect printed mass-shift unit and uninspected supplementary spectra require further assessment; condition-specific negative antiport results are not universal nonfunction.

discussions.notes: Do not transfer Upf0118 antiport to TqsA or collapse the four E. coli family members. Retain the LB biofilm decrease, glucose-dependent regulation, possible deletion pleiotropy and lack of established AI-2-specific mediation. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve direct TqsA transport and assay-specific mediators before extending reporter effects into a molecular pathway.
discussions.rationale: The historical knockout/rescue data support scoped cellular effects but do not distinguish enhanced export from inhibited uptake, and structure/binding does not by itself establish transport.
